evidence.note: After naming Peleg as one of Eber’s two sons, the verse names his brother Joktan.
Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, and Jerah.

article.name: יָקְטָן
article.summary: Eber’s two sons are Peleg and Joktan. The genealogy lists Joktan’s sons beginning with Almodad. The meaning of Joktan’s name is uncertain.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for יָקְטָן. Leave the root unassigned because the genealogy gives no evidence for the proposed derivation from יקה.
draft.definition: Joktan, son of Eber and brother of Peleg.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:25 identifies Joktan as Peleg’s brother. Genesis 10:26 names Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, and Jerah among his sons.

analysis.evidence: In וְיָקְטָן יָלַד אֶת אַלְמוֹדָד, Joktan is the father and אֶת marks Almodad as the first child named. The genealogy identifies Joktan but gives no derivation for his name.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ, “and,” prefixes the masculine personal name יָקְטָן. Joktan is the subject of the third-person masculine singular verb יָלַד, “fathered.”
analysis.sense: Joktan, the son of Eber and brother of Peleg

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68120:1, 68120:5, 68111:1, 68109:1, 68104:1, 66578:5, 66578:9, 66578:13.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks the proper name אַלְמוֹדָד as the direct object of יָלַד, “fathered.” Each following וְאֶת introduces another son whom Joktan fathered.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

evidence.note: The genealogy opens Joktan’s list of sons with יָלַד אֶת אַלְמוֹדָד, “he fathered Almodad.”

article.name: אַלְמוֹדָד
article.summary: Almodad is the first son named in Joktan’s genealogy, followed by Sheleph, Hazarmaveth and Jerah.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for Almodad and correct the occurrence’s temporal gloss to “Almodad.”
draft.definition: Almodad, the first son named in the list of Joktan’s sons.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:26 names Almodad immediately after “Joktan fathered.”

analysis.evidence: In וְיָקְטָן יָלַד אֶת אַלְמוֹדָד, Joktan is the subject of יָלַד, “fathered,” and אֶת introduces Almodad as his son. The repeated וְאֶת introduces each of the following names.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no attached prefix or suffix. The preceding אֶת is a separate direct-object marker.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for שֶׁלֶף. The genealogy identifies the bearer but leaves the name’s derivation uncertain.
draft.definition: Sheleph is the personal name of a son of Joktan.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:26 names Sheleph as the second object of “Joktan fathered.”

analysis.evidence: In Genesis 10:26, יָקְטָן is the subject of יָלַד, “fathered.” The repeated object marker אֶת introduces each son in turn, placing שָׁלֶף between Almodad and Hazarmaveth.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal proper noun. The pausal form שָׁלֶף has qamats in place of the lemma’s first segol. The preceding וְאֶת is a separate word.

draft.change: Add Genesis 10:26 as evidence for the existing definite-object sense of word 0.
draft.definition: Introduces a definite direct object, here a personal name in a coordinated list.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 10:26, וְאֶת חֲצַרְמָוֶת adds Hazarmaveth to the named objects of יָלַד.

analysis.evidence: In וְאֶת חֲצַרְמָוֶת, וְ adds Hazarmaveth after Sheleph in the list of sons Joktan fathered. אֶת introduces his name as the third object of יָלַד, “fathered.”
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וְ means “and.” אֶת is the unsuffixed direct-object particle.
analysis.sense: Marks Hazarmaveth as a definite direct object of יָלַד.

analysis.evidence: Joktan is the subject of יָלַד ‘fathered’. The repeated object marker אֶת introduces each child's name, placing Hazarmaveth between Sheleph and Jerah.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix. The preceding וְאֶת is a separate word.
analysis.sense: Personal name of a son of Joktan.

analysis.evidence: וְיָקְטָן יָלַד introduces Joktan as the father. The repeated object marker אֶת introduces each child's name, and the final וְאֶת יָרַח identifies Jerah as the fourth child listed in this verse.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name in the verse-final pausal form יָרַח, with no prefix or suffix.
